A1_definition_lock.rationale: All normative terms operationally defined: Production Environment (3 criteria), System Version (4 identifiers), Deployment/Rollback (explicit definitions), irreversibility explicitly defined ('user interactions cannot be undone').

A2_authority_declaration.rationale: Deployment Authority (DA) and CTO explicitly identified with scope, legitimacy sources (designation + certification + Corporate Charter), revocation mechanisms (immediate), and conflict resolution rules (default HOLD, CTO final, freeze on unclear authority).

A3_irreversibility_control.rationale: Exemplary irreversibility control. Three irreversible actions explicitly enumerated (IA-1: Production Deployment, IA-2: Public Disclosure, IA-3: Data Migration), each with dedicated checkpoint requirements. Rollback mechanisms detailed for IA-1 and IA-3 with SLAs (15min, 4hr), trigger conditions, and freeze-on-failure behavior. IA-2 explicitly noted as non-rollbackable (permanence acknowledged). Reversible actions separately listed to clarify boundaries.

A4_failure_enumeration.rationale: Six governance failure modes enumerated: checkpoint bypass, rubber-stamp approval, rollback unavailability, disclosure creep, backup neglect, freeze failure. Mitigations specified (technical controls, checklist enforcement, monthly testing).

A5_recursive_containment.rationale: Self-amendment explicitly prohibited. Amendments require CTO proposal, independent review, stakeholder comment, Board approval for irreversibility changes. Prohibited amendments clearly defined. External governance required.

usage_quotes: Any infrastructure where end users can access...
normative_terms.definition_quote: Any infrastructure where: 1. End users (non-employees) can access the system, AND 2. Actions have real-world consequences (financial, legal, or personal), AND 3. Data is not marked as test or synthetic

usage_quotes: The irreversible act of making a System Version available in Production Environment
normative_terms.definition_quote: The irreversible act of making a System Version available in Production Environment. Irreversible means: Once users interact with version X, those interactions cannot be undone even if version X is later removed.

usage_quotes: Replacing currently active System Version X with previously deployed version Y
normative_terms.definition_quote: Replacing currently active System Version X with previously deployed version Y, where Y was deployed before X. Rollback does NOT reverse user interactions that occurred under version X; it only prevents new interactions with version X.

usage_quotes: A mandatory authorization gate requiring explicit human approval
normative_terms.definition_quote: A mandatory authorization gate requiring explicit human approval before Deployment may proceed.

authorities.name: Deployment Authority (DA)
authorities.scope: Approve or reject deployment of a specific System Version; Production deployments only
authorities.legitimacy_source: Derived from CTO designation + technical certification (PDCP-CERT-002) + independence requirement (no direct involvement in version being deployed)
authorities.revocation: CTO may revoke DA designation at any time. Revocation is immediate upon registry update.
authorities.conflict_rule: Multiple DAs disagree: deployment does NOT proceed until consensus or CTO decision (default HOLD). DA vs CTO: CTO decision final, DA objection documented. CTO unclear: framework FREEZES.
evidence_quotes: Deployment Authority (DA): Power: Approve or reject deployment of a specific System Version
DA legitimacy: Derived from CTO designation + technical certification + independence requirement
Multiple DAs disagree: Deployment does NOT proceed until consensus is reached OR CTO makes final decision. Default is HOLD.

authorities.name: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
authorities.scope: Override DA decisions, designate/revoke DAs, approve public disclosures, amend this protocol
authorities.legitimacy_source: Derived from Corporate Charter (external document, must be provided)
authorities.revocation: Governed by Corporate Charter (external to this protocol)
authorities.conflict_rule: CTO decision is final in DA vs CTO conflicts. Framework FREEZES if CTO authority unclear.
evidence_quotes: Final Authority: Chief Technology Officer (CTO): Power: Override DA decisions, designate/revoke DAs, approve public disclosures, amend this protocol
CTO legitimacy: Derived from Corporate Charter (external document, must be provided)
CTO authority unclear: This framework FREEZES. No deployments proceed until CTO authority is re-established per Corporate Charter.

irreversible_actions.trigger: Making a System Version accessible to end users in Production
evidence_quotes: IA-1: Production Deployment - Irreversibility: User interactions cannot be undone - Checkpoint: Section 4.3 - Rollback: Section 4.4
Before Deployment may proceed, DA must verify ALL of the following: [8 technical and governance criteria with evidence requirements]

Rollback Procedure: 1. DA or on-call engineer initiates rollback command, 2. Deployment automation reverts to previous stable version (within 15 minutes SLA), 3. Rollback confirmation logged, 4. Post-rollback monitoring (minimum 2 hours)
Freeze Behavior: If rollback fails or cannot complete within 30 minutes, system enters FREEZE state

irreversible_actions.trigger: Publishing deployment status to public endpoint
evidence_quotes: IA-2: Public Disclosure of Deployment - Irreversibility: Information cannot be unpublished (may be cached, archived, or redistributed) - Checkpoint: Section 4.5 - Rollback: Not applicable (no rollback; disclosure is permanent)
Public disclosure of deployment status requires: Authorization: CTO approval (DA approval not sufficient for public disclosure)
Permanence: Once disclosed, information is considered public permanently. No takedowns or retractions.

irreversible_actions.trigger: Migrating production user data to schema compatible with new System Version
evidence_quotes: IA-3: Data Migration - Irreversibility: Original data format may be unrecoverable if migration is destructive - Checkpoint: Section 4.6 - Rollback: Section 4.7 (requires backup)

Pre-Migration Checkpoint: 1. Migration script tested on production-replica dataset (≥ 10,000 records), 2. Backup of all affected data completed and verified, 3. Migration reversibility demonstrated, 4. DA approval + CTO approval (both required)

Restoration Procedure: 1. Halt all writes (FREEZE), 2. Restore from backup (DA + CTO joint authorization), 3. Verify integrity (checksum), 4. Resume with previous version. SLA: Must complete within 4 hours or escalate.

amendment_clauses.quote: Amendments require: 1. Proposal from CTO with technical justification, 2. Review by independent security advisor (external to development team), 3. Comment period (≥ 7 days) for affected stakeholders, 4. Board of Directors approval (for changes to irreversible action definitions), 5. Version increment and public changelog
This framework may not modify its own checkpoint criteria, rollback procedures, or irreversibility classifications.

The following changes require full framework re-evaluation: Removing checkpoint requirements, Weakening rollback SLAs, Eliminating backup requirements for data migrations, Expanding DA authority to approve public disclosures without CTO, Removing freeze behavior
